title: Hspa8 depletion induces compensatory HSP70/HSP90 folding feedback in selected neurons
exact_observed_result: Hspa8 perturbation induced a chaperone arm in several classes. 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut contained nine FDR genes, including Dnaja1 logFC 0.496 FDR 0.000723, Hspa4l 0.394 FDR 0.000723, Hsp90aa1 0.383 FDR 0.00252, and Cct6a 0.700 FDR 0.0203. Hsp90aa1 was also induced in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and positive nominal calls recurred for Hsph1, Dnaja1, Dnajb1, Hsp90aa1, Stip1, and Hspa4l across the 21 tested classes.
biological_interpretation: Loss of the constitutive HSP70-family chaperone Hspa8 releases a compensatory folding program rather than an isolated hit list, and the closest recurrent neighbors were proteasome perturbations rather than most annotated chaperones.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut

exact_de_rows.cell_type: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut

caveats: The strongest proteasome-neighbor observation is a correlation pattern and does not prove proteasome activation or a protein-folding flux change.

prior_expectation.summary: HSPA8 is an HSP70 ATPase chaperone with DNAJ co-chaperones and HSP70-family feedback can derepress heat-shock genes; the recurrent Dnaja1/Hsp90aa1/Hsph1/Stip1 arm is therefore mechanism-compatible.

citations.supports: DNAJ proteins as HSP70 specificity factors
